subject: Re: Streaming chat p99 spike during peak — urgent escalation
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@fixly.com>

Subject: Streaming chat p99 spike tonight (SSE) — noticed ~19:00 PST

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing very high tail latency (p99) on the SSE streaming chat endpoint starting ~19:00 PST — roughly when our user traffic spiked for a promotional push. Impact: several customer sessions timed out and our internal retries amplified request volume. I've attached a screenshot of our observed p95/p99 over the hour and a tiny request log snippet.

Quick facts:
- Endpoint: /v1/streams/chat (SSE) on hosted.redwoodapi.com
- Time window: 2026-09-18T18:55–19:25 PST
- p95 rose from ~120ms to 750ms, p99 hit ~2.6s for ~18 minutes
- Error rate (5xx) increased from 0.04% to 0.9% in the same window

This is customer-impacting for Fixly Pro users. Please escalate — we need a mitigation and timeline.

Thanks,
Sara Lopez
Customer Success Manager
Fixly

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-18T19:22:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: Fixly SSE p99 regression during 19:00 peak — immediate triage requested

Team — Fixly (Fixly Pro) is seeing a p99 surge on the hosted SSE streaming chat endpoint during last night's promo spike. Customer attached metrics and a short log snippet (attached above). They reported: p95 ~750ms, p99 ~2.6s, and 5xx uptick. This is affecting sessions and causing retries.

Please treat as urgent:
1) Confirm whether this is an autoscaler/concurrency boundary or a model runtime KV cache miss.
2) Check recent deploys or config changes in the last 24 hours (routing, batching, quantization profiles).
3) Recommend an immediate mitigation we can apply to reduce tail latency (route to lower-latency model variant, reduce batch window, pre-warm workers, adjust autoscaler thresholds).
4) I need a short mitigation we can communicate to the customer within 20–30 min and an ETA for a durable fix.

CC: Markus for exec visibility.

Thanks — Vanessa

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-18T19:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Fixly SSE p99 regression during 19:00 peak — initial findings

On Sep 18, 2026, at 19:22, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com wrote:
> Team — Fixly (Fixly Pro) is seeing a p99 surge on the hosted SSE streaming chat endpoint...

Quick initial triage:
- Correlated metrics show a spike in request concurrency at 18:58 PST that aligns with Fixly's promo.
- We observed higher-than-normal average sequence lengths for those sessions (~1.7x baseline) which increased KV cache pressure.
- Autoscaling lag: the Dedicated routing pool for hosted shared tier hit the concurrency cap and scaled after ~3 minutes, causing queuing and elevated tail latency.
- There were no recent model code deploys or kernel changes in the last 24h; however, a config tweak to batching window for streaming (made as an experiment for other customers last week) lowered throughput headroom for short bursts.

Immediate mitigations we can apply now (fastest first):
A) Route Fixly traffic to a pre-warmed dedicated variant with higher concurrency limits (expected p99 drop to <600ms within ~6 minutes).
B) Temporarily reduce the streaming batch window to prioritize latency over throughput for the Fixly route (instant but may increase token cost).
C) Increase autoscaler aggressiveness for the shared pool (will reduce lag but take ~3–6 minutes to spin up).

I've attached a 60-line request log snippet and a small graph (sse_request_snippet_19_10.log, fixly_p99_chart_20260918.png). My recommendation for customer communication: apply A + B immediately, monitor 5–10min, then allow C to stabilize.

Longer-term action items being proposed:
- Revert the experimental batch-window change or gate it per-customer by workload pattern.
- Add an early-warning alert for sequence-length-driven KV pressure.
- Add automatic temporary routing to dedicated variant on spike detection for high-SLA customers.

I'll start the route change now if you approve.

— David
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

1) Routing Fixly traffic to a pre-warmed dedicated variant (expected improvement within ~6 minutes).
2) Reducing the streaming batch window for the Fixly route to prioritize latency.

We expect p99 to fall below ~600ms after step 1 completes and verification. David will monitor and report back in 10 minutes.

Call scheduled at 20:05 PST to confirm and to provide an exec summary. We're treating this with high priority and will follow up with an RCA and a customer-facing summary.

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll share credits/compensation options post-incident.

— Vanessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@fixly.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T23:05:00-07:00
Subject: FINAL RCA (draft) — Fixly SSE p99 spike 2026-09-18

Summary (sendable to customer after review):
- Impact window: 2026-09-18T18:58–19:18 PST.
- Root cause: workload spike + increased sequence lengths led to KV cache pressure and queuing while autoscaler reacted; an experimental reduction in streaming batch headroom amplified the queuing effect for short traffic bursts.
- Mitigation performed: 1) Temporary routing to a dedicated pre-warmed variant; 2) Reduced batch window for Fixly route; 3) Increased autoscaler aggressiveness until steady-state. These actions restored p99 to baseline within ~10 minutes.

Quantified impact: peak p99 ~2.6s, average error rate bump to 0.9%, affected 4.2% of Fixly Pro sessions in the 20-minute window.

Follow-ups / action items:
- Roll back the experimental batching change and re-evaluate per-workload gate (owner: infra config team, ETA 2 weeks).
- Implement an automatic temporary route-to-dedicated policy for high-SLA customers when spike detection triggers (owner: routing team, ETA 3 weeks).
- Add an alert for high sequence-length KPIs and KV cache pressure (owner: monitoring, ETA 1 week).
- Provide customer credits and a short exec-level incident summary (owner: sales ops, ETA 48 hours).

Next steps: Vanessa — recommend we send the short RCA + compensation offer to Fixly this morning and offer a 30-minute review call for their execs. Markus — flagging for visibility; we can propose a minor credit and a goodwill consult on peak preparation.

Attachments: mitigation_playbook_v1.md (internal playbook for identical spike patterns).

— David
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
